findings.evidence: Spanning.lean:233-235 `def indCharacterSet (𝒮) := {f | ∃ S ∈ 𝒮, ∃ n ρ, ρ.IsIrreducible ∧ ind S (ofCharacter ρ) = f}`; Spanning.lean:247 `noncomputable def indCharacterSpan (𝒮) := Submodule.span k (indCharacterSet k G 𝒮)`; Artin.lean:139-141 uses the same `indCharacterSet` under `AddSubgroup.closure`, and its own docstring states the difference is that "its coefficients are integers".
findings.fix: Name it after the coefficient ring, e.g. `indCharacterSpanInt` (or `indCharacterAddSpan`), matching `indCharacterSpan` and letting the `Int`/`Add` token carry the difference; update the four dependent names (`ind_ofCharacter_mem_…`, `…_le_iff`, `…_le_indVirtualCharacters`, `indVirtualCharacters_eq_…`) accordingly.
findings.issue: `indIrreducibleCharacterSpan k G P` is `AddSubgroup.closure {f | ∃ χ ∈ indCharacterSet k G {C | P C}, ↑χ = f}` — the ℤ-closure of exactly the generating set of the existing `indCharacterSpan k G 𝒮 = Submodule.span k (indCharacterSet k G 𝒮)`. The names differ by the token `Irreducible`, but `indCharacterSet` already consists of characters induced from *irreducible* characters, so the name advertises a distinction that does not exist and hides the one that does (coefficient ring ℤ vs `k`, and `AddSubgroup (G → k)` vs `Submodule k (ClassFunction k G)`). A reader will take it for the irreducible-character part of `indCharacterSpan`.

findings.evidence: Ideal.lean:128-132 `indVirtualCharactersAddHom (P) : DirectSum {S // P S} (fun S ↦ ↑(virtualCharacters k S)) →+ virtualCharacters k G := DirectSum.toAddMonoid fun S ↦ indVirtualCharactersOfSubgroupAddHom k G S`; VirtualCharacter.lean:124-129 `indVirtualCharactersOfSubgroupAddHom (S) : virtualCharacters k S →+ virtualCharacters k G`; ClassFunction.lean:172 `def indClassFunAddHom (S)` and VirtualCharacter.lean:79 `private def compSubtypeAddHom (S)` bundle functions of the same base name.
findings.fix: Put the direct sum in the name of the direct-sum map and drop the misplaced qualifier: `indVirtualCharacterDirectSumAddHom` / `indVirtualCharacterDirectSumBaseChangeRat` for the family map, and `indVirtualCharacterAddHom` for the single-subgroup map; rename the derived lemmas to match.
findings.issue: `indVirtualCharactersAddHom k G P` has domain `⨁_{S // P S} R(S)`, but its name carries no direct-sum marker, while the simpler single-subgroup map `indVirtualCharactersOfSubgroupAddHom k G S` (VirtualCharacter.lean:124) carries the extra qualifier `OfSubgroup` — the qualification runs backwards, and both are "of subgroups". Additionally, the `⟨fn⟩AddHom` pattern in this repo means "that function bundled" (`indClassFunAddHom`, `compSubtypeAddHom`), whereas `indVirtualCharacters` is an `AddSubgroup`, so `indVirtualCharactersAddHom` is not the bundling of `indVirtualCharacters`. The headline theorem `indVirtualCharactersBaseChangeRat_surjective_isCyclic` states surjectivity of `ℚ ⊗ ⨁_C R(C) → ℚ ⊗ R(G)`, which its name does not convey. Same instance at Ideal.lean:173 (`indVirtualCharactersBaseChangeRat`) and Ideal.lean:136/148 (`indVirtualCharactersAddHom_of`, `range_subtype_comp_indVirtualCharactersAddHom`).

summary: Two naming problems: `indIrreducibleCharacterSpan` distinguishes itself from the existing `indCharacterSpan` by a feature both share (irreducibility) instead of by the actual difference (ℤ vs `k` coefficients), and the two new bundled induction maps are named so that the direct-sum map carries no marker of the direct sum while the single-subgroup map carries the extra qualifier.
